summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Lucia Dolce served at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015), and at Minobusan University as visiting researcher (attested 2026).
Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and later held a post there.

Lucian Scherman worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and earned his PhD under Ernst Kuhn at Munich. He held professorships at the University of Munich (1901–1933) and directed the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907–1933).

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught Italian at Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Bernot was a scholar of Tibetology and sinology who studied at INALCO and EPHE. He held posts at CNRS (1947–1964), EPHE (1961–1978), and served as Professor of “Sociographie de l’Asie du Sud-Est” at Collège de France (1979–1985).

Working in philosophy and religious studies, Lucien Lévy-Bruhl studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He held a post at the University of Paris (~1899–1927) and founded the Institut d'ethnologie.

Linguist Lucien Tesnière studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig, ENLOV, and under Antoine Meillet. He held appointments at the University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), University of Ljubljana (~1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).

Linguist Lucjan Malinowski studied at Jagiellonian University, Uniwersytet Petersburski, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Jena. He served as professor of Slavic philology at Jagiellonian University from ~1877 to 1898.
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

Ludo Rocher, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned doctorates at Ghent University and studied under Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda. He was a professor at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and later chaired South Asia studies at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002).

Linguist Ludvig Frands Adalbert Wimmer studied at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, obtaining his MA and PhD. He then served at Copenhagen as PD (1871), Docent (1875), and Professor of Nordic Philology (1886–1910).

Ludwig Alsdorf worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD under Walther Schubring at Hamburg and habilitating under Heinrich Lüders in Berlin. He held posts in Berlin and Münster before serving as professor of Indian history and culture at Hamburg (1950–1978).

Ludwig Bachhofer, an art historian specializing in Indology and sinology, earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Lucian Scherman. He served as Privatdozent at Munich (1927–1935) and later as Assistant Professor of Art at the University of Chicago (1935–1965).

Ludwig Diestel was a scholar of religious studies who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic posts at the universities of Bonn (~1858–1862), Greifswald (~1862), Jena (~1862–1872), and Tübingen (~1872–1879).

Ludwig Fritze, an Indologist, studied at Lehrerseminar Oranienburg (1851–1854). He pursued a teaching career at Lehrerseminare in Oranienburg (1861–1871), Zabern (1871–1873), Drossen (1873–1885), and Köpenick (1885–1906).

Ludwig Heinrich Kapff was an Indologist and scholar of religion who earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen. He worked as a Privatdozent at Tübingen (1830–1833), rector at Karlsgymnasium Heilbronn (1843), and Ephorus at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (1854–1869).

Ludwig Heller, an Indologist and linguist, earned his doctorate under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen and habilitated at Greifswald. Following work at the Royal Library of Berlin, he became a professor of Indology at the University of Greifswald (1904, full professor 1920).

Ludwig Lange studied at Göttingen and Leipzig under Theodor Benfey and Karl Friedrich Hermann. A scholar of linguistics and classical philology, he was professor at Charles University (1853–1859), University of Giessen (1859–1871), and University of Leipzig (from 1871).

Ludwig Oster was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Richard Pischel and completed his PhD at Heidelberg University under Christian Bartholomae and Salomon Lefmann.

Ludwig Poley was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin and Eugène Burnouf and Silvestre de Sacy in Paris. He held teaching posts at the University of Padua (1866) and the University of Vienna (1867).
